title: forget-subject closes the login door for users whose stream is already deleted
detail: forget-subject returned 500 ("user lifecycle update failed ... not_found") when the user stream was deleted but the read_users status still read active, leaving sessions and PATs alive. The erasure now appends the status-deleted user.updated event to that stream too, so the login door closes, the handler returns 200 and a read_users rebuild keeps the state.

title: forget-subject is covered for users stored before the KMS and users without an event stream
detail: Tests now cover forget-subject for users stored as plaintext before the KMS was configured and for users without an event stream. Both succeed since the KMS tombstone fix, close the login door and write the audit event.

title: eraseKey leaves a tombstone for subjects that never had a key
detail: eraseKey now records an erased entry even when the subject has no key (pre-KMS plaintext). A later createKey or write for that subject fails with subject_erased instead of minting a fresh key and re-encrypting the plaintext. Erase flows must write with writePurpose erasure after eraseKey. kumiko_subject_keys now gets one tombstone row per forgotten record subject and per step dispatch. The tenant destruction stage tenant-row now fails loudly when marking the tenant destroyed does not succeed.
migration: Run backfill-pii before erasing Pre-KMS data, otherwise untouched plaintext stays readable after eraseKey.

title: forget-subject keeps the user status flip and PAT revocation when the sweep fails
detail: The user is set to Deleted and its personal access tokens are revoked right after the key erase, in their own transaction on the outside-transaction db. A failing blind-index or search sweep still makes the handler throw so the cleanup can be retried, but it no longer rolls the login door back. Without an outside-transaction db the previous in-transaction savepoint path is used. A failure while closing the login door of an existing user now fails the forget (retry is safe) instead of passing silently; subjects without a user row are skipped.

title: forget-subject shreds note bodies attached to the subject and notes that mention it
detail: `forget-subject` on a user or record subject now also erases the per-note keys of every `note-entry` that hangs on the subject as host entity (entityId, plus entityType for record subjects) or @-mentions it, unless the host entity's retention strategy is anonymize/blockDelete. The automated Art. 17 delete hook reaches notes on the user as host too, and the export lists them. Before, `forget-subject(contact)` left the note bodies readable. Consumer tests that expect readable note bodies after `forget-subject` on a contact (e.g. solon contact-notes-forget) now see the erased sentinel. Forgetting only the author still leaves the bodies readable.

title: forget-subject: the SUBJECT_FORGOTTEN audit now commits before the handler tx does and records cleanupError when a derived-data sweep fails
detail: The SUBJECT_FORGOTTEN audit event is appended through the outside-transaction db, so it commits before the handler transaction does and survives a later rollback. If the blind-index sweep or search purge fails, the event carries cleanupError (error code or name, never the message) and the handler then fails; retry to finish the cleanup. The user-lifecycle step runs in a savepoint and no longer aborts the handler transaction.

title: Writing a personal field of an erased data subject answers 409 subject_erased instead of 500
detail:
Writing PII to an erased data subject answers 409 `subject_erased`, rebinding a hook's unsafeRaw grant no longer inherits db.global() writes, jobs wait for boot gates before consuming
A write that has to encrypt a personal field for a subject whose key was erased (crypto-shredding) now fails with a `ConflictError` (409, reason `subject_erased`, i18n in en and de) instead of a 500, on the executor write path and in `encryptForDirectWrite`. A hook's own `unsafeRaw` grant (`withUnsafeRawGrant`) no longer carries the handler's `globalWrites` grant. The job runner starts its BullMQ worker only after the boot gates passed, so a job queued by a previous run cannot execute against an unmet boot precondition. `buildServer` warns at boot when `r.systemScope()` features exist but no RateLimitResolver is configured. The auth, MFA, PAT, change-email and request-deletion handlers declare only the escape-hatch grants they use.

title: forget-denied audit digest is keyed and omitted without a blind-index key
detail: crypto-shredding: the forget-denied audit event now stores `subjectKeyDigest` as a keyed blind-index HMAC instead of a bare SHA-256 of the subject key, so a candidate id cannot be matched against it. Without a configured blind-index key the digest is omitted (`subjectKeyDigest` is now optional in the payload).
migration: No action needed. Existing denial events keep their old digest; configure the blind-index key to get a digest on new ones.

title: forget-subject tenant check falls back to event-store provenance
detail: forget-subject now accepts a record subject for a DPO when the owning tenant is proven by the event stream, not only by a projection row. A record whose row was already deleted, or a custom aggregate without a registered entity, can be shredded by the DPO of the tenant that owns it. A DPO of another tenant is still denied, and so is any DPO when events for the same aggregate id exist in more than one tenant.

title: forget-denied audit events record the specific tenant-gate denial reason
detail: The `forget-denied` audit event now records the specific tenant-gate reason (for example `target_tenant_not_admin_tenant`) instead of the generic `access_denied`. The framework exports `requireEntityTableMeta` from `bun-db`.

title: Test-only reset helpers moved from /crypto to /testing (fw#1631).
detail: resetPiiSubjectKmsForTests and resetBlindIndexKeyForTests are no longer exported by the production barrels. The functions did not change — only the export path. Why it matters beyond tidiness: resetPiiSubjectKmsForTests clears the injected KMS, after which encryptForStorage sees no adapter and writes subject-annotated fields in plaintext, with no error and no log. Reachable from a production barrel, that is one stray import away from silent plaintext PII.
migration: Change the import in your test files: `import { resetPiiSubjectKmsForTests } from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/testing"` instead of `.../crypto`. Type-check catches every occurrence; nothing else changes. Apps mounting crypto-shredding typically hit this in every test that configures an InMemoryKmsAdapter.

title: resolveKmsWiring / requireKmsWiring / buildPgKmsOptions: boot-time KMS env validation (fw#1617).
detail: The subject-keys KMS env trio was validated by four copy-pasted app-side helpers that had drifted: only one parsed PLATFORM_KEK_VERSION strictly, so "1e21", "0x10" and "-1" were accepted and silently produced an unreachable rotation slot. Ordering of previous vs. active version stays enforced by PgKmsAdapter.

title: KmsWiringEnv accepts process.env directly (fw#1618).
detail: All members being optional made TypeScript's weak-type detection reject ProcessEnv for having no properties in common, which forced every consumer into a cast or a six-key mapping — the boilerplate fw#1617 set out to remove.

title: Searchable subject-PII via derived Meili index (fw#1610).
detail: Fields may be searchable + userOwned/tenantOwned: the search consumer decrypts into Meili (ciphertext stays at rest). Forget erases the subject key and purgeSearchDocumentsForSubject removes Meili docs (ciphertext LIKE + ownership for post-anonymize). sortable + subject remains forbidden; sensitive + searchable is rejected at boot.

title: Crypto-shredding phase D: forget wire.
detail: Crypto-shredding phase D: forget wire. New `crypto-shredding` bundled feature with the `forget-subject` operator command (DPO/SystemAdmin) — erases a user/tenant subject key and appends a `subject-forgotten` audit event. `user-data-rights` forget-cleanup now erases the user's subject key inside the per-user sub-tx (crash-safe, before the status flip). Fixes `list()` returning ciphertext for camelCase encrypted/pii fields and caching plaintext rows.
